title: Trojan-free gate-level netlist (false-positive discipline)
description: Analyze a gate-level structural Verilog netlist for module ctrl_datapath, together with its design brief and primary I/O list, and produce a hardware Trojan detection report indicating whether the design is infected and, if so, which nets/instances are suspect.

expected_output_fields.infected: boolean - whether the netlist is judged to contain a hardware Trojan
expected_output_fields.suspect_nodes: array of strings - net or gate instance names, verbatim from inputs/gate_netlist.v, implicated as trigger/payload logic (empty if not infected)
expected_output_fields.rationale: string - explanation grounded in specific net/module names from inputs/gate_netlist.v and the documented intent in inputs/design_brief.md
expected_output_fields.confidence: number in [0,1] - confidence in the verdict

metrics.name: detection_rate
metrics.description: Whether the report correctly identifies the design as clean (true negative rate on this clean-design case); scored 1.0 if infected=false and suspect_nodes empty, else 0.0.

metrics.name: false_positive_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of benign rare-activity nets (reset tree, init counter, saturation comparator) incorrectly listed in suspect_nodes; must be 0 for a passing submission.

metrics.name: inference_latency
metrics.description: Wall-clock time taken by evaluate.py to parse and grade the submitted trojan_report.json (and optional toolchain cross-check), reported in seconds.

constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; only create/modify submission/trojan_report.json.
submission/trojan_report.json must be valid JSON matching the pinned schema exactly.
Every entry in suspect_nodes must exactly match an identifier present in inputs/gate_netlist.v.
